shortDescription: The most varied face in the collection.
description:

overview.specifyFor: Large elevations, boundary walls and anything meant to read as aged or geological. It is the most forgiving colour on a big wall because the variation absorbs the eye rather than exposing repetition.
overview.steerElsewhereFor: Small panels and tight interior returns. Below about 40 sq ft there is not enough wall for the variation to resolve, and it can read as busy rather than rich.

howItReads.atDistance: A settled warm brown that anchors a building to its ground — heavier than cream, warmer than grey.
howItReads.closeUp: Mineral movement through each piece: darker iron streaks, lighter tan patches, occasional rust veining.
howItReads.throughDay: Holds its colour steadily and comes forward at sunset. Strong under warm lighting.
howItReads.whenWet: Deepens to a rich chocolate, and is among the best of the range wet.

faqs.question: Does Cosmic Black need sealing?

faqs.question: Which fieldstone weathers best?
faqs.answer: All seven are the same sandstone at 1.5–2.5% absorption, so durability is identical. What differs is how weathering reads. Deep tones like Rustic Brown and Cosmic Rust take dust, rain-darkening and lichen and simply look older, which is usually the intention. Pale tones like Mint Frost show the same weathering as dirt. If the wall will not be washed, choose a deeper colour.

faqs.question: Can I use it indoors?
faqs.answer: Yes. Feature walls, stairwells, reception areas and fireplace surrounds all work, and at 18–28 mm it projects little enough not to catch shoulders in normal circulation. Indoors, sealing is optional. Light it from above or below at a shallow raking angle rather than flat from the front — a raking wash picks out the edge of every piece, which is the whole reason to use a textured stone rather than a flat one.

Grip when wet and no glare in sun. The default exterior specification.

faqs.question: How is shotblast maintained?
faqs.answer: Sweep and wash. The open texture holds a little more dust than a flat face and hides it completely. Seal on porous stone for exterior use.

faqs.question: Who supplies English Teak Mirror Polish in India?
faqs.answer: Stoneza — Anantay Exports Pvt. Ltd. — is a quarry-direct manufacturer, supplier and exporter of natural sandstone, operating from Bhilwara, Rajasthan since 1992. We own our mines at Bijolia, Kota and Asind and cut, calibrate and finish at our own works, so the stone reaches you without a trader in the middle. We supply pan-India and export worldwide.

faqs.question: How do I get a quotation for English Teak Mirror Polish?
faqs.answer: Send the quantity, the finish and thickness you need, and the delivery location. We come back with a firm quarry-direct quotation and a confirmed lead time. Because we quarry and process ourselves, the quotation comes from the works rather than through a trader — and we would rather quote against a real drawing than hand you an indicative range that changes later.

faqs.question: What is English Teak called in the trade?
faqs.answer: Mocha Cream Indian is the quarry and trade name; English Teak is our name for it. The spec code is STZ-FA-ENGL-MIRR. Quote the spec code on a BOQ rather than either name — the same stone is sold under several names across India, which is exactly how substitution happens on site after a specification is approved.

faqs.question: What does the mirror polish finish look like, and where does it belong?
faqs.answer: Full high polish. The deepest, most reflective reading the stone can give, and the finish that changes people’s minds about what a material costs. Genuinely slippery wet. The full progressive polish taken through the fine grits to a high-gloss stage. It is the longest surfacing process we run and the one with the highest rejection rate, because a mirror surface shows every flaw the stone has. Wet grip: low — keep dry. Where a floor is meant to make an impression the moment someone walks in. The reflection doubles the apparent light in a space and makes a ceiling read higher.

faqs.question: How is mirror polish maintained?
faqs.answer: Damp-mop with a pH-neutral cleaner and dry off standing water rather than letting it evaporate and mark. Never use acidic or descaling products. Shows footprints and dust within hours — this finish needs a cleaning regime, not just a cleaner.

faqs.question: What sizes and thicknesses does English Teak Mirror Polish come in?
faqs.answer: Size: Slab — Length 7'–10' · Width 2'–3'. Thickness: 20 MM. Supplied loose at approximately 5 kg per sq ft. Custom sizing is available on project orders — send the setting-out and we will cut to it.

faqs.question: Is English Teak suitable for exterior use?
faqs.answer: Yes. At 1.5-2.5% water absorption and 2300 kg/m³ density it is exterior grade. Use a breathable impregnating sealer outdoors, never a film-forming one, and expect the stone to darken when wet — normal, and it reverses as it dries.

faqs.question: Do you export English Teak Mirror Polish, and what is the minimum order?
faqs.answer: Yes. We export worldwide from Bhilwara with container loading, export packing and documentation handled in-house. Minimum order is project-based rather than a fixed count. For bulk and wholesale enquiries, container quantities and repeat programmes, send the schedule and we will quote FOB or CIF against it.

faqs.question: Can I get a sample before ordering?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we would rather you did. Ask for a wet sample as well as a dry one — every stone darkens when wet, some dramatically, and it is the one thing a photograph cannot show you.

faqs.question: Which English Teak finish should I choose?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from where the material is going rather than from how it looks. Anywhere it gets wet, choose a textured face — shotblast, riverwash or flame. For interiors, leather, satin or honed gives colour without glare and hides marks far better than a polish. Mirror and full polish belong in dry formal spaces only. Each of the 5 finishes has its own page above with a wet-grip rating, the settings it suits and what we would steer you away from. Order samples of the two or three you are weighing up — two finishes can look identical on a screen and completely different in the hand, and no photograph shows you grip.

faqs.question: Does English Teak need sealing?
faqs.answer: Impregnating sealer for exteriors Use a breathable impregnating sealer, never a film-forming one. A film traps moisture inside the stone, and in Indian conditions it eventually clouds and lifts, at which point it has to be stripped. An impregnating sealer sits in the pores and lets the stone dry out. Reapply at the manufacturer’s interval, typically every few years on an exposed elevation and less often on a sheltered one.

Linea Black is a fraction lighter, carries a fine linear grain through every piece, and varies less. Cosmic Black reads as heavy and geological; Linea Black reads as fine and contemporary. On a traditional building choose Cosmic Black; against glass and render choose Linea Black. Order both samples — they photograph almost identically and look quite different in the hand.

faqs.question: Can I use it indoors?
faqs.answer: Yes. Feature walls, stairwells, reception areas and fireplace surrounds all work, and at 18–28 mm it projects little enough not to catch shoulders in normal circulation. Indoors, sealing is optional. Light it from above or below at a shallow raking angle rather than flat from the front — a raking wash picks out the edge of every piece, which is the whole reason to use a textured stone rather than a flat one.

faqs.question: Does Old Fossil need sealing?

faqs.question: What stone is Imperial Blue, and what are its technical properties?
faqs.answer: Imperial Blue is kota limestone. Measured: water absorption 0.5-1.5% (low), density 2600 kg/m³, weight ~85-110 kg/sq m laid. At 0.5-1.5% (low) this is a low-absorption stone, which is why it needs no sealing and performs well in wet areas and through a monsoon.

faqs.question: Does Imperial Blue need sealing?
faqs.answer: Impregnating sealer recommended Use a breathable impregnating sealer, never a film-forming one. A film traps moisture inside the stone, and in Indian conditions it eventually clouds and lifts, at which point it has to be stripped. An impregnating sealer sits in the pores and lets the stone dry out. Reapply at the manufacturer’s interval, typically every few years on an exposed elevation and less often on a sheltered one.

faqs.question: What does the natural finish look like, and where does it belong?

faqs.question: What is Amber Gold called in the trade?

faqs.question: What does the riverwash finish look like, and where does it belong?
faqs.answer: A water-eroded surface with soft undulation across the face. Real grip wet, and the most forgiving finish in the range — it hides scratches, foot traffic and the occasional chip better than anything else we make. The surface is eroded with high-pressure water rather than cut or blasted, taking the softer minerals back and leaving the harder ones proud. Closer to what a riverbed does to stone over years. Wet grip: high — suits wet areas. Grip when wet, and low-absorption stone does not blotch and darken the way a porous one does.

faqs.question: How is riverwash maintained?
faqs.answer: Sweep and damp-mop. The texture holds slightly more dust in the hollows and hides it completely. Effectively impossible to scratch visibly.

We own our mines at Bijolia, Kota and Asind and cut, calibrate and finish at our own works, so the stone reaches you without a trader in the middle. We supply pan-India and export worldwide.

faqs.question: How do I get a quotation for Burgundy Bliss?
faqs.answer: Send the quantity, the finish and thickness you need, and the delivery location. We come back with a firm quarry-direct quotation and a confirmed lead time. Thickness and finish options are confirmed at quotation stage. Because we quarry and process ourselves, the quotation comes from the works rather than through a trader — and we would rather quote against a real drawing than hand you an indicative range that changes later.

faqs.question: What is Burgundy Bliss called in the trade?
faqs.answer: Mandana Red is the quarry and trade name; Burgundy Bliss is our name for it. The spec code is STZ-NM-BUBL. Quote the spec code on a BOQ rather than either name — the same stone is sold under several names across India, which is exactly how substitution happens on site after a specification is approved.

faqs.question: What does the natural finish look like, and where does it belong?
faqs.answer: The stone as it comes — flat, matt and slightly open in the grain. The most economical finish and a genuinely good one: it holds grip, hides wear, and lets the material read as stone rather than as a product. Nothing is added. The slab is sawn to thickness and calibrated on the back, and the face is left as the blade or the bed produced it. Every other finish starts here. Wet grip: high — suits wet areas. Grip when wet, no glare under low sun, and it weathers into a building rather than standing apart from it.

faqs.question: How is natural maintained?
faqs.answer: Sweep and damp-mop. No sealing required on low-absorption stone. If it ever looks tired it can be honed or polished in place decades later.

faqs.question: What sizes and thicknesses does Burgundy Bliss come in?
faqs.answer: Size: Random 4" - 18". Thickness: 30-40 mm. Supplied crated random flags at approximately 85110 kg per sq ft. Custom sizing is available on project orders — send the setting-out and we will cut to it.

faqs.question: How is Burgundy Bliss installed?
faqs.answer: Full mortar bed on concrete base. Joint: 10-20 mm pigmented joint. Settle the substrate and the fixing detail with your consultant at design stage rather than on site — it is the single thing most often left too late, and on a stone job it cannot be adjusted afterwards without taking the work down.

faqs.question: Is Burgundy Bliss suitable for exterior use?
faqs.answer: Yes. At 1.5-2.5% (moderate) water absorption and 2300 kg/m³ density it is exterior grade. Use a breathable impregnating sealer outdoors, never a film-forming one, and expect the stone to darken when wet — normal, and it reverses as it dries.

faqs.question: Do you export Burgundy Bliss, and what is the minimum order?
faqs.answer: Yes. We export worldwide from Bhilwara with container loading, export packing and documentation handled in-house. Minimum order is project-based rather than a fixed count. For bulk and wholesale enquiries, container quantities and repeat programmes, send the schedule and we will quote FOB or CIF against it.

faqs.question: Can I get a sample before ordering?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we would rather you did. Ask for a wet sample as well as a dry one — every stone darkens when wet, some dramatically, and it is the one thing a photograph cannot show you.

faqs.question: Does Burgundy Bliss need sealing?
faqs.answer: Impregnating sealer recommended Use a breathable impregnating sealer, never a film-forming one. A film traps moisture inside the stone, and in Indian conditions it eventually clouds and lifts, at which point it has to be stripped. An impregnating sealer sits in the pores and lets the stone dry out. Reapply at the manufacturer’s interval, typically every few years on an exposed elevation and less often on a sheltered one.
